extracted.intended_audience: individuals seeking registration/limited recognition to practice before the USPTO (patent agents, attorneys, former Office employees), and practitioners subject to USPTO practice rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing admission/registration to practice before the USPTO, limited recognition, moral character and reputation investigations, post‑employment restrictions, administrative suspension/inactivation, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility for former patent examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: A former patent examiner may have the registration examination waived if they meet specified service, rating, and disciplinary history requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (i) two complete fiscal years as a patent examiner in the Office; (ii) rated at least fully successful in each quality performance element for the last two complete rating periods; and (iii) not under an oral or written warning regarding quality performance elements at time of separation. See related paragraphs for timing and fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility for certain former Office employees (non-examiners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may waive the registration exam for a former Office employee who demonstrates by petition comprehensive knowledge of patent law equivalent to passing the exam and necessary legal qualifications to render valuable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may include positions providing substantial guidance on examination policy, development of rules/procedures, MPEP changes, training/testing materials, representation of the Office before federal courts; and ratings of at least fully successful in quality performance elements for the last two complete rating periods and not being under warning at separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing to be considered for waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for waiver consideration, a former employee in specified categories must file a complete application for registration and pay the §1.21(a)(1)(i) fee within two years of separation from the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former employees who file more than two years after separation must take and pass the registration examination. If non-waiver is notified, the individual must pay the exam fee within thirty days after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination results finality and limited review rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of registration examination results is final; within 60 days of mailing a notice of failure, the individual may inspect (but not copy) the questions and answers they answered incorrectly under supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notes may be taken during review. Substantive review of answers or questions may not be pursued by petition for regrade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee for reciprocal recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual seeking reciprocal recognition under §11.6(c) must, in addition to satisfying eligibility provisions, pay the application fee required by §1.21(a)(1)(i) upon filing for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal recognition applicants must satisfy paragraphs (a) and (b) of the section and §11.8(b) as well as pay the stated fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure duty in registration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant must answer all questions in the registration application and requests for information; disclose all relevant facts, dates, and provide verified copies of documents relevant to good moral character and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys should submit certified copies of State bar applications and determinations of character and reputation, if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED investigation when adverse information received
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED receives information adverse to an applicant's good moral character or reputation, the OED Director will conduct an investigation after the applicant has passed (or been waived from) the exam as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely answer questions or respond to an inquiry results in deemed withdrawal of the application; no certification until the OED Director is satisfied the individual demonstrates good moral character and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed withdrawal for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual failing to timely answer questions or respond to an OED inquiry is deemed to have withdrawn the application and must reapply, pass the examination, and satisfy all requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of prior progress; timely response to OED inquiries is mandatory during investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of State bar determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may accept a State bar's determination of character and reputation for an attorney-applicant if, after review, the Office finds no substantial discrepancy between the State bar materials and the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is discretionary and contingent on consistency between documents and the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence showing lack of good moral character and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of evidence that may show lack of good moral character include conviction of specified felonies/misdemeanors, drug or alcohol abuse, lack of candor, suspension or disbarment on ethical grounds, and resignation from a State bar while under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is illustrative, not exclusive; OED evaluates the totality of an applicant's record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction presumption and ineligibility periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Conviction of a felony or certain misdemeanors results in a presumption the individual lacks good moral character absent a pardon or satisfactory showing of reform; such individuals are ineligible to apply during sentence/probation/parole and for two years after completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court record of conviction is conclusive evidence in absence of pardon or satisfactory showing of reform. Upon applying, convicted individuals must file specified fees and provide satisfactory evidence of rehabilitation for OED determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility upon reversal or set-aside of conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conviction has been set aside or reversed, the individual may be eligible to file a complete application and fees; upon passing the exam, the OED Director will determine whether, absent the conviction, the individual possesses good moral character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-aside or reversal does not automatically restore eligibility; OED makes a final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug or alcohol abuse evaluation and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Records are reviewed as a whole for drug/alcohol abuse; an individual appearing to abuse may be asked to undergo an evaluation (at their expense) by a professional approved by the OED Director; OED may request withdrawal if there is present abuse or no record of recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested to withdraw, the applicant must later demonstrate compliance with treatment and recovery to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of candor as basis for denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to candidly disclose facts relevant to moral character or reputation in the application or thereafter may be cause to deny registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full and truthful disclosure is mandatory; omissions or misstatements are judged seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of disbarment, suspension, or resignation in lieu
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant disbarred, suspended on ethical grounds, or who resigned in lieu of discipline is ineligible to apply for specified periods: five years for disbarment/resignation; until suspension expiry for suspension. Additional criminal convictions extend ineligibility as set elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file full records of disciplinary proceedings, pay fees, and provide satisfactory proof of good moral character upon reapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions from disciplinary records
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the record resulting in disbarment, suspension, or resignation is prima facie evidence of the matters contained and the imposition of discipline; the imposition is conclusive that professional misconduct occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such records create strong presumptions and govern determinations of character and eligibility during the period of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited defenses to underlying disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The only defenses to an underlying disciplinary matter (disbarment, suspension, resignation in lieu) that will be considered are: lack of notice/opportunity to be heard (deprivation of due process), infirmity of proof sufficient to doubt the Office accepting the conclusion, or that Office finding would result in grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden is on the applicant to show one of these narrow defenses to overcome disciplinary presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in determining rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve guideline factors to evaluate rehabilitation include nature of misconduct, applicant's age/education at time and present, time elapsed since misconduct, restitution, expungement, completion of probation, abstinence from substances for not less than two years where implicated, treatment for mental disease if applicable, payment of fines, correction of behavior, social benefit involvement, and change in attitude evidenced by statements from the applicant and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors are illustrative and used to assist the OED Director; no single factor is determinative—consideration is holistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to show cause procedure for moral character issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED finds the applicant has not satisfactorily established good moral character, it issues a notice to show cause; the individual has no less than ten days from the notice date to reply (certified mail in U.S., other reasonable means outside U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receipt of response (or absence), OED considers the record and decides whether the applicant sustained the burden of proof. Procedural timelines and service methods are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication following refusal or withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual refused registration for lack of good moral character may reapply two years after the decision (unless shorter period ordered); an individual who withdrew while under investigation may reapply two years after withdrawal. Reapplicants must pay fees and again satisfy moral character and exam requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if previously passed the exam, reapplicants must complete the examination successfully upon reapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of status from agent to attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent registered under §11.6(b) requesting registration as an attorney under §11.6(a) must demonstrate their good standing as an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good standing proof (e.g., certificate) is required; procedural details are in §11.6 and §11.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath, data sheet, and fee filing deadline after passing or waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: After passing the exam or receiving a waiver, the applicant must, within two years of mailing the notice of passing or waiver, file a completed Data Sheet, an oath/declaration prescribed by the USPTO Director, and the registration fee under §1.21(a)(2). Attorney applicants must also provide a certificate of good standing not more than six months old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply within two years requires retaking the registration examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition — scope and ineligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited recognition may be granted to non-registered individuals to prosecute specified patent application(s) upon showing necessity/justification and good moral character; limited recognition does not extend beyond specified applications and is not granted to individuals who have passed the exam or had it waived while their registration application is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition based on immigration status is conditioned on U.S. authorization to work or train and is time-limited consistent with immigration authorization; will terminate if immigration status or authorized employment ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition — application and qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive limited recognition, an applicant must apply on OED form, furnish requested information and materials, and establish to OED satisfaction that they possess good moral character, legal/scientific/technical qualifications to render valuable service, and competence to advise and assist in presentation and prosecution of applications. They must also pass the registration examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete application includes form, payment of §1.21(a)(1) fees, satisfactory proof of scientific/technical qualifications, and proof that immigration terms authorize relevant employment/training. Each limited recognition seeker must take and pass the registration exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination retake limits and waiting periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual failing the registration exam may reapply; waiting periods: 30 days after last attempt for first or second failure; 90 days after last attempt for third or fourth failure. An individual may not take the exam more than five times absent a petition to waive this limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon reapplying, applicants must file a complete application form, pay fees, provide proof of authorized immigration/employment if applicable, and provide proof of good moral character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application handling and cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete applications for limited recognition will not be admitted to the examination and will be notified of deficiencies. Applications with deficiencies may be considered only if cured within 60 days of the mailing date of the notice; thereafter, a new complete application is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cure within 60 days means starting anew; filing complete applications each time is essential for admission to the exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of admission scheduling and extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: OED sends a notice of admission specifying a period to schedule and take the exam. An applicant may request an extension in writing before expiration and pay the §1.21(a)(1)(iv) fee; granted requests extend the scheduling period by 90 days. Failure to take the exam within the period requires filing a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions must be timely requested and paid for; after expiration without taking the exam, reapplication is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of limited recognition after expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A person whose limited recognition expired less than five years prior may be reinstated if they file a complete application including required proofs (fees, immigration authorization, moral character). Persons whose recognition expired five years or more earlier must comply and also provide objective evidence that they continue to possess necessary legal qualifications to render valuable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement standards are stricter after longer lapses; objective evidence of continued qualifications is required if five years or more have passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on who may represent others before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Only practitioners registered under §11.6, individuals given limited recognition under §11.9(a) or (b) or §11.16, or individuals admitted pro hac vice under §41.5(a) or §42.10(c) are permitted to represent others before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized representation is prohibited; check registration/recognition status before acting for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment undertaking for former Office employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Former Office employees who practice after termination must sign a written undertaking not to knowingly act as agent/attorney/design patent practitioner for any person before the Office in connection with any particular patent/application in which they participated personally and substantially as an Office employee, and (separately) must not knowingly act within two years after termination for any patent/application that was pending under their official responsibility in the one year prior to termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The undertaking imposes both absolute (any participation) and time-limited (two-year) restrictions tied to prior involvement and responsibility; contractual compliance is required to practice post-employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information update and biennial registration statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners (and those with limited recognition under §11.9(b)) must notify the OED Director of office postal address, one to three email addresses, business telephone number, and every change within thirty days. Biennially they may be required to file a registration statement to confirm active status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the registration statement or provide requested information within specified times may subject the practitioner to administrative suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative suspension notice and cure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner fails to comply with the registration statement requirement, OED will publish and send a notice demanding compliance and payment of a delinquency fee within 60 days; failure to comply leads to a notice to show cause and possible administrative suspension after procedural steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices are sent to the last addresses/e-mails on record; practitioners must timely comply or respond to avoid suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative suspension process and practitioner response rights
rubrics_metrics.description: After a notice to show cause is sent, the practitioner has 30 days to file a response addressing factual and legal bases why they should not be administratively suspended. OED may file a reply within 10 days. The USPTO Director will enter an order suspending the practitioner if no genuine issues of material fact exist about noncompliance, otherwise dismiss the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reconsideration must be filed within 20 days of the decision. Suspension cannot be stayed during review. If OED withdraws the notice before the Director issues an order, suspension will not occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and discipline while administratively suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner is prohibited from practicing before the Office in patent matters while administratively suspended and may be subject to discipline for conduct before, during, or after the suspension period. Knowing practice while suspended is itself subject to discipline under §11.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administratively suspended practitioners may request reinstatement by complying with reinstatement requirements in §11.11(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment by the Office leads to administrative inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner who becomes employed by the Office must withdraw from representations, notify the OED Director in writing on the first day of employment, and will be endorsed as administratively inactive; upon separation they may request reactivation per §11.11(f)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners employed by the Office are removed from active practice rosters and remain subject to the Rules of Professional Conduct and disciplinary proceedings for prior conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary inactivation and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registered practitioner may voluntarily enter inactive status by written request; upon acceptance the name is endorsed as voluntarily inactive. Voluntarily inactive practitioners are prohibited from practicing before the Office and remain subject to investigation and discipline for conduct prior to, during, or after inactivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance of voluntary inactive status, the practitioner must comply with §11.116 regarding withdrawal from matters.
